claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing natural gas distribution business (T4) and its three operating divisions crossed intact, but shared corporate-service processes (IT, accounting/internal-controls, treasury/risk, tax, environmental, telecommunications) did NOT transfer as an intact operating substrate — ONE Gas was "developing a plan" to replace such services — creating a documented product-vs-process mismatch at closing. gap_mitigated=yes: this substrate gap was contractually absorbed at closing via a Transition Services Agreement (plus Separation/Distribution, Tax Matters, Employee Matters, and Management agreements) providing costs-only bridging services. gap_56=0: the operating divisions crossed intact alongside their ~3,100 employees and experienced management team, so processes moved together with the people/organization that run them.

gemini.rationale: The customer-facing business (T4) and its operating divisions (T5) transferred intact, so there is no gap_45. However, certain corporate functions (IT, treasury, tax, etc.) did not transfer as an intact operating substrate, creating a gap_56 where the organization (T6) transferred but some operational processes (T5) were left behind. This gap was mitigated at closing by a Transition Services Agreement.

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 because the customer-facing regulated distribution business (T4) and its three operating divisions crossed intact and continued as divisions of ONE Gas, so product and core delivery processes moved together at closing. gap_56=0 because management and approximately 3,100 employees historically associated with that business also crossed into ONE Gas under the Employee Matters Agreement, aligning organization with the transferred operations. Shared corporate-service substrate (IT, treasury/risk, tax, environmental, telecom) that did not transfer whole was bridged by a Transition Services Agreement, but that bridging does not constitute a T4-vs-T5 or T5-vs-T6 structural mismatch for the core business tiers.
